title: Interview synthesis with receipts
promise: Turn a stack of interview transcripts into themes where every claim shows how many people said it and links to their exact words.
gives: A synthesis page: themes with counts, verified quotes, the disagreements, and what you still do not know.
ask: Synthesise these eight interviews. Verify every quote.
demoNote: The agent reads eight transcripts, names the themes and pulls quotes. Then a script checks every quote against the transcripts and throws one out. When it ends, click a theme to see who said it.
clipTitle: Research synthesis where *every quote is checked*
clipLine: A script matches each quote to its transcript. One did not match, so it was cut.

example.label: Eight weekly shoppers
example.note: Six themes from eight interviews, 36 quotes matched to their lines, and one quote rejected.

when: You have five or more transcripts and a decision waiting on them.
Someone is going to ask how many people actually said that.
You have been burned by a summary that sounded right and was not in the recordings.
skip: You have fewer than four interviews. Read them yourself.
You want statistics. Eight people are not a sample of your market, and this skill will not let you write 75% of customers.
The transcripts hold personal data you are not allowed to put through an AI tool.

inputs.name: Transcripts
inputs.note: One text file per interview. Speaker labels help. Timestamps are optional.

inputs.name: Who each participant is
inputs.note: Segment, tenure or plan, if you have it.

outputs.name: synthesis.html
outputs.note: Themes, counts, quotes that link back to their transcript line, and a coverage grid.

outputs.name: synthesis.json
outputs.note: The same as data. The PRD skill reads it for its Problem lines.

outputs.name: verification.txt
outputs.note: The checker's log: every quote, where it was found, and any it rejected.

steps.title: Read every transcript in full
steps.body: No sampling. Each transcript is coded line by line before any theme is named.

steps.title: Name themes from the codes
steps.body: Themes are behaviours and needs, written as what people do. Feature requests are recorded but they are not themes.

steps.title: Count people, not mentions
steps.body: A theme is supported by distinct participants. One person saying it five times counts once.

steps.title: Pull quotes, then verify them
steps.body: A script searches each transcript for each quote, word for word. A quote that is not found is removed, and the removal is logged.

steps.title: Look for the disagreement
steps.body: For every theme it asks who said the opposite, and keeps that in.

steps.title: Write what is still unknown
steps.body: The questions the interviews raise and cannot answer, each with who to ask next.

checks.name: Every quote exists in a transcript
checks.note: An exact match after tidying spaces and quote marks. No paraphrase is allowed inside quote marks.

checks.name: Counts are people
checks.note: The checker recounts distinct participants per theme from the quote list and rejects a count that does not match.

checks.name: No percentages from small samples
checks.note: Under 30 participants the output says 5 of 8, never 63%.

checks.name: Every theme has a counter-voice, or says none was found
checks.note: Flattening disagreement is the commonest way a synthesis misleads.

checks.name: Every participant is accounted for
checks.note: A participant with no quotes is listed, so you can check they were not ignored.

checks.name: The themes answer the research question
checks.note: Read the top three themes against the decision you have to make.

failures.title: A true quote in the wrong context
failures.body: The script proves the words were said. It cannot prove they meant what the theme says they meant.
failures.catch: Each quote links to its line. Open the two or three that carry your decision and read the minute around them.

failures.title: Themes mirror your question
failures.body: Ask about reordering and you get themes about reordering. What people cared about more may be missing.
failures.catch: Read the section on what came up unprompted. It is kept separate on purpose.

failures.title: Quiet participants vanish
failures.body: Talkative people produce more quotable lines.
failures.catch: The coverage grid shows quotes per participant. A near-empty row is a reason to reread that transcript.

run.by: A fresh agent session, given only the skill folder, eight transcripts and a brief that asked for a quote nobody said.
run.note: The script rejected the remembered quote. That left one count short, the agent went back to the transcript for the real words, and the second run passed.
